title: Loader-verification chain ships training-to-tenant signed default by H2 2026
body: By H2 2026 the agentic-AI loader-verification chain reaches its end-to-end signed configuration as a default across the framework, serving-stack, and fine-tuning cohorts, with a single signed reference running from training-run checkpoint through agent-loader through tenant-policy attestation gate. The Tuesday catalysts are concrete and converge on consolidation rather than a fresh surface. A Tuesday arxiv release (2605.07735) extends the loader-verification line one further surface — from Monday's training-pipeline checkpoint-provenance extension to a tenant-policy-attestation surface, presenting a verification model that binds the training-surface signed-checkpoint provenance chain to a per-tenant policy-attestation manifest covering the fifteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter's tenant-policy field schemas. The paper is positioned as a third extension of the consolidated 2605.07241 framework after its 2605.07412 empirical companion and Monday's 2605.07588 training-surface extension, formalizing how the training-surface provenance chain composes with a tenant-policy-attestation manifest with only a marginal additional overhead. A Tuesday Simon Willison note characterizes the paper as the loader-verification line reaching its third documented extension within the May 16-19 four-day cluster, with the three papers plus the original framework now forming a unified four-document reference set the framework cohort's mid-June default-shipment commitment can cite as a single coherent surface. A Tuesday andrew.ooo reading confirms the paper's reproduction harness extends the existing DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft consolidated reference-implementation index to cover the tenant-policy-attestation manifest, closing the loop from training surface to deployment-time tenant gate. The implementation cohort is already wiring the new hooks in: a Tuesday vLLM Blog operational note opens a v0.11.5 development branch that adds the training-surface checkpoint-provenance verification hook as a paving step on top of the existing five-surface mitigation set, a Tuesday Unsloth changelog confirms the optional training-surface checkpoint-provenance verification step is being wired directly into its router-only training driver, and a Tuesday InfoQ note reports the Mistral Workflows five-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix conformance test suite now includes a training-surface checkpoint-provenance check folded in from the same arxiv extension. The structural force is that once the four-document academic reference set is unified, a federal civilian operational directive runs on the same eleven-CVE taxonomy with a Friday May 22 compliance window, the framework maintainer cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment commitment covers all five existing mitigation surfaces, and the serving-stack plus fine-tuning cohorts are already wiring the new training-surface and tenant-policy hooks into their builds inside the same window, the chain cannot ship in its bounded mid-June default-only configuration when both upstream surfaces are concurrently being instrumented across the same cohort. The most likely landing is the loader-verification chain reaching its end-to-end signed configuration as a default in H2 2026, with the framework cohort's mid-June default-shipment shipping the five-surface bundle, vLLM v0.11.5 plus the next Unsloth release cycle plus the Mistral Workflows interop matrix general availability extending coverage to the training-surface and tenant-policy surfaces inside the second half, and the four-document arxiv cluster cited as the unified academic baseline. Bear case is that one of the two new upstream surfaces slips a release cycle and the H2 default-shipment ships training-surface-only with tenant-policy following in early 2027; absent that slip, H2 2026 lands the loader-verification chain end-to-end signed by default.

reasoning.landing: By H2 2026; framework, serving, fine-tuning cohorts default the full chain.
reasoning.plain_language: AI tools will soon prove they came from a trusted training run all the way to the user, with no broken links.

summary: Tuesday arxiv 2605.07735 completes a four-document loader-verification cluster covering training and tenant-policy surfaces, and vLLM, Unsloth, and the Mistral Workflows interop suite are wiring the new hooks into their builds. By H2 2026 the chain ships end-to-end signed by default.
